question: to the Commission Pernando Barrena Arza (The Left) Subject:

In 2025, the EU installed 65.1 GWDC of solar photovoltaic (PV) capacity, a 0.7 % decline from 2024 and the first such contraction in a decade. Total capacity reached 406 GWDC, meeting the 2025 target of 400 GWdc (320 GWAC). However, SolarPower Europe forecasts further declines, to below 62 GWDC in 2026 and 60 GWDC in 2027. Consequently, the EU would reach around 718 GWDC by 2030, falling short of the 750 GWDC (600 GWAC) target and only slightly above the 701 GWDC aggregated in Member States’ national energy and climate plans (NECPs). The slowdown is driven by policy rather than technical constraints. Residential rooftop solar declined from 28 % of new capacity in 2023 to 14 % in 2025 after several Member States ended support schemes without replacement. Corporate power purchase agreement contracting also fell 41 % between the first and second quarters of 2025 amid negative price events. Meanwhile, power demand remains below 2019 levels, weakening electrification incentives. 1.
What measures will the Commission take in response to the first contraction of the EU solar market in a decade?
How will the Commission ensure that the EU reaches the 750 GWDC target by 2030 given current trends and Member States’ lower NECP ambitions?
Is the Commission planning a framework for storage, hybridisation and residential rooftop solar to address these market weaknesses?
